lines: Welcome back to the podcast.
Today my guest is a nurse who became a software engineer at forty five.
Thanks so much for coming on.
Thank you, I'm a little nervous, to be honest.
So take us back, what made you switch careers?
I was on a night shift, and a patient's chart was wrong.
The system had copied an old allergy into the wrong record.
We caught it with about ten minutes to spare.
I went home and couldn't sleep.
I kept thinking, somebody wrote that code, and nobody checked it.
So I signed up for a coding class the next morning.
My kids thought I'd lost my mind.
My daughter actually helped me with my first Python homework.
That's beautiful.
What was the hardest part?
Honestly, believing I was allowed to be there.
Everyone in the bootcamp was half my age.
On day three I cried in the parking lot.
And then on day four I came back.
Now I build the safety checks for hospital software.
The exact kind of check that would have caught that chart.
If you're listening and you think it's too late for you, it isn't.
Before we go, where can people find you?
I'm on LinkedIn, just search my name.
